_rascunho: Draft translation of the Portuguese text (pt.json is the final one).
lead: To talk on Alumia with the encrypted chat, use the phone or computer app. The chat code ships inside the app: what runs on your device does not come from the server every time you open it. And every version is recorded in a public log that anyone can check.

soApp.texto: The website has the social network. The encrypted chat runs in the phone or computer app, with the code inside it and every version recorded in a public log.

baixar.iphone: There is no iPhone app yet. iPhone users keep chatting on the website while the website chat is open.
baixar.semVersao: No version has been published yet. When there is one, it shows up here, with the digest of each file and its entry in the public log.

conferir.texto: Every app file is signed by the release workflow of the Institute's public repository, on a version tag, and recorded in Rekor, Sigstore's public signature log. Nobody holds a key that could sign on the side: the signature comes from the workflow's identity, and the log makes each one public forever.
passos: Download the file and its verification bundle (the file with the same name ending in .sigstore.json).
Check it with one of the commands below. Both tell you whether the file is exactly what the workflow signed and whether the signature is in the log.
Only install if the check passes. If it fails, do not install and tell the coordination.
conferir.comandoNode: With the repository code (Node 22 or newer):
conferir.roteiro: Guide to build the app from scratch and get the same file
conferir.trocar: Replace {versao} with the version and {arquivo} with the file name.

sistema.texto: The app does not have Microsoft's or Apple's paid signature. That is why the system warns that the program comes from an unknown source. Trust comes from somewhere else: the public log and the reproducible build. Check the digest before opening it.

atualizacao.texto: The app only installs an update that is in the public log, signed by the repository's release workflow. Outside the log, it refuses and says why. A version installed some other way that is not in the log opens, but the chat does not.
